result:
**Verdict: FAIL.** I found two Medium defects that count as mandatory violations (data integrity and access control). Both were reproduced through the real API on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 database.

I confirmed the candidate before starting: HEAD was 2c22c27 and the candidate ID matched `sha256:25c97340…863061b` (391 files). HEAD later moved to 3c85e91, which only adds the domain reviewer's run files; the candidate ID did not change. I read no other reviewer's records.

**Required checks** (all run in a throwaway clone, since removed):
- **Passed:** typecheck, build, lint, `openapi:lint` (33 operations), no-CDN, formatting, the SBOM check and the historical DG0 validation.
- **Unit tests:** Node 24 passed 325/325. On Node 22 the first run failed one test (324/325); three reruns passed 325/325.
- **Integration suite:** run twice; 200/200 both times, with 8 migrations applied to a fresh database.
- **Tooling tests:** gate/agent tooling 105/105, deploy scripts 59/59.
- **CI:** all three `ci.yml` copies are byte-identical and every product job depends on `delivery-gates`.
- **REQ-S16-001:** API and worker run as separate processes. After stopping the worker, the API still answered `/healthz` and `/readyz` with 200.
- **Installer suite (REQ-DLV-042):** 13 of 14 acceptance checks pass offline. The 14th ("AC-1 effect") installs a package from the npm registry, which is unreachable here, so it failed. The online install effect is **not verified**. As the assignment and D-057 asked, I recorded it as the disclosed residual rather than as a separate BLOCKED check, and said so plainly in the record. I also had to give pnpm a writable copy of its package store, because HOME is read-only in my sandbox.

**Findings** (proposed IDs; the orchestrator may renumber):

| ID | Severity | Mandatory | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG1-140 | Medium | yes | Two concurrent "move business unit" requests both return 200 and save a loop in the hierarchy (A→C→B→A). The no-loops rule is only an application check that two requests can pass at once (`organization/routes.ts:335-376`), with nothing in the database behind it. Moving one at a time is correctly refused. |
| F-DG1-141 | Medium | yes | Moving a business unit checks permission on the unit being moved, never on the new parent. A manager scoped to unit a1 moved a1x under sibling unit a2, where they have no rights. An auditor scoped to a2 then went from 404 to 200 on a transformation that sits under a1x. |
| F-DG1-142 | Medium | no | The global rate limit keys on any session cookie the client sends, valid or not (`server.ts:128-131`). Sending a new random cookie each time gave 50 requests and no 429 at all, versus a 429 on the 4th request with no cookie. Login routes have their own per-IP limit and are not affected. |
| F-DG1-143 | Low | no | The module-boundary lint (ADR-0002) can be bypassed through the allowed `ajv` package, whose code-generation helper runs arbitrary JavaScript. My test file reached `child_process` and imported `access/policy.ts` directly, with zero lint violations and every check still green. `ajv`, `ajv-formats` and `yaml` are only used by tests but are listed as runtime dependencies, so they also ship in the production image. |
| F-DG1-144 | Low | no | One web test is intermittent (`transformations.test.tsx:528`, default 1-second wait); it failed 1 of 4 Node 22 runs. |
| F-DG1-145 | Low | no | The ERD and data dictionary don't document the three views the authorization model relies on (`scope_node`, `business_unit_closure`, `actor_display`). `schema.ts` also points to a test file that doesn't exist. |
| F-DG1-146 | Low | no | D-057 says the installer suite passes 14/14 offline; it actually passes 13/14 offline (AC-1 effect needs the registry). |

**Files written:**
- `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-1/code-security-reviewer.json`: the review record; it and the findings sidecar validate against the gate schemas, and all evidence paths exist.
- `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-1/code-security-reviewer.findings.json`: the findings above.
- `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-1/code-security-reviewer.md`: a short narrative.
- `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-1/`: all logs and reproduction tests. The reproductions were only ever run in throwaway copies.
